titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§125–130: Chinggis Qan's Thanks, the Kereid Seal, and Jamuqa's Defeat
part: §§125–130 — Chinggis Qan's Thanks, the Kereid Seal, and Jamuqa's Defeat
about: Six sections. §125 has Chinggis, now qan, thank Bo'orchu and Jelme for their company and set them over the rest, naming each man to his post. §126 sends Daqai and Sükegei to To'oril Qan of the Kereid, whose answer is that Temüjin should be qan and that the compact must not be broken. §127 is the message sent to Jamuqa and Chinggis's envoys' reply to Altan and Quchar, who had made him qan and parted him from his anda. §128 tells how Jamuqa's younger brother Taichar took Jüchi-Darmala's herd and was shot dead for it. §129 follows the war: Jamuqa and the thirteen Jadaran come, Chinggis meets them at Dalan-Baljut and falls back to the Cherene gorge, and Jamuqa boils the Chinos princes. §130 tells how the Uruqud and Mongqud and old Münlig leave Jamuqa for Chinggis, and how a feast on the Onon ends with a beaten cook. The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan qān bolžu Boγ̇orču, Želme qojar-a ügülerün:"

morph.gloss: there, then (locative adverb, from tere 'that') [那裏]
Chinggis, a man's name (personal name; the name taken by Temüjin) [(太祖︀)]
qan, ruler (the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: There Chinggis Qahan qan becoming, Bo'orchu, Jelme two-to on-speaking:
sentences.i: There Chinggis Qahan, now qan, said to Bo'orchu and Jelme, the two of them:
sentences.n: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan qān bolžu is 'there Chinggis Qahan, becoming qan' (Ming 做着, the converb): the qan now speaks as qan. qojar-a (Ming 兩箇行) is 'to the two', summing up the pair named before it; the comma after Boγ̇orču is Shiratori's. Shiratori's quotation mark opens on the next word and runs on to the end of the section's speech.

sentences.t: Ta qojar nama-ji seġüder-eče busu nökör ügei-dür seġüder bolžu sedkil min-u amuγ̇ulba že ta;

morph.gloss: me (bi 'I', oblique stem nama-) [我 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
without, there is not [無 時]
dative-locative: at, in (front-vowel form); after ügei, 'when there is not'
genitive ending, set after its noun

sentences.l: You two me-than shadow-than other companion without-when, shadow becoming, heart my set-at-rest, indeed you;
sentences.i: "You two set my heart at rest, becoming my shadow when I had no companion but my shadow;
sentences.n: Ta qojar nama-ji is 'you two, me': the Ming 我行 marks nama-ji as an object, but the verb takes sedkil min-u 'my heart' as its object, so nama-ji is probably 'for me'. seġüder-eče busu nökör ügei-dür is 'when there was no companion other than the shadow' (Ming 除影兒別伴當無時): the ablative -eče does the work of 'than', and ügei-dür is 'in the absence of'. amuγ̇ulba is amu- 'peace' + causative -γ̇ul- + -ba, 'caused to be at peace' (Ming 敎安了); the stem is inferred. že ta, 'indeed, you', closes the clause. The grammar of the first half is clear; the sense of 'becoming a shadow' (Ming 影兒做着) is a figure, I take it, for sticking close beside him.

sentences.t: sedkil-dür atuγai" keġebe.

morph.gloss: optative, third person: 'let it be, may it ...'

sentences.l: Heart-in let-it-remain" he-said.
sentences.i: Keep it in your hearts," he said.
sentences.n: atuγai is a- 'be, remain' with the optative -tuγai: 'let it remain' (Ming 存者). Whose heart it is, the Ming does not say: sedkil-dür follows ta; and so I read 'in your heart', the heart of the two being addressed. The closing mark after atuγai and the stop after keġebe are Shiratori's; the next speech begins with a new opening mark.

sentences.t: "Seġül-eče busu čičuγ̇a ügei-dür seġül bolžu žirüge min-u amuγ̇ulba že ta;

morph.gloss: without, there is not [無 時]
dative-locative: at, in (front-vowel form); after ügei, 'when there is not'
heart (a second word for 'heart', beside sedkil) [心]
genitive ending, set after its noun
peace, rest (stem inferred from the Ming 安) [安了]
particle, 'indeed, so' (the Ming 也者 'so be it') [也者︀]

sentences.l: "Tail-than other whip without-when, tail becoming, heart my set-at-rest, indeed you;
sentences.i: "You set my heart at rest, becoming my tail when I had no whip but a tail;
sentences.n: The speech repeats the first with a different figure: seġül-eče busu čičuγ̇a ügei-dür is 'when there was no whip other than the tail' (Ming 尾子處別鞭子無時), and seġül bolžu 'becoming the tail'. The Ming 尾子 'tail' is not explained, and what a horse's or a man's tail stands for as a whip (a following, or the thing behind him) I cannot say; I give the words and do not guess. žirüge is a second word for 'heart', beside sedkil; the Ming 心 glosses both alike.

sentences.t: čeġeži dotora min-u atuγai" keġebe.

morph.gloss: genitive ending, set after its noun
optative, third person: 'let it be, may it ...'

sentences.l: Breast inside my let-it-remain" he-said.
sentences.i: Keep it within my own breast," he said.
sentences.n: čeġeži dotora min-u atuγai: 'breast within my let-it-remain' (Ming 胷懷內我的敎存者). The Ming reads it as 'let it remain within my breast'; whether the speaker asks them to keep his words, or to let their service remain with him, the line does not say. I give 'keep it' as a plain reading.

sentences.t: "Ta qojar urida baiγsaγ̇ar ede bükün-i aqalažu ülü-ü aqun ta" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to stand, to be set up (stem inferred from the Ming 立) [立了的上頭]
past participle -γsan with instrumental -ar: 'because of having ...ed' (the Ming 上頭 'on account of')
all, those who are (from bü- 'to be'; Ming 有的 'those existing') [有的 行]
makes a verb from a noun: to act as, to do with ...
particle of question (uncertain; the Ming puts its 麽 on the next word)
ending of the verb (uncertain; the Ming 住麽 reads it as a question, 'will you dwell?')

sentences.l: "You two earlier because-of-having-stood these existing-ones elder-being not-? dwell you," he-said.
sentences.i: "Since you two stood by me first, will you not stay as elders over all of these?" he said.
sentences.n: baiγsaγ̇ar is bai- 'stand, be set up' + past participle -γsan + instrumental -ar, 'because of having stood' (Ming 立了的上頭 'on account of having stood'): they stood by him first. ede bükün-i is 'these, all who are' (Ming 這的每有的行). aqalažu is aqa 'elder' + -la- + -žu, 'being elder, taking the place of the elder' (Ming 爲長着). ülü-ü aqun ta: ülü 'not', -ü perhaps the question particle, aqun 'dwell, stay'; the Ming 不住麽 asks 'will you not stay?'. The ending of aqun is not settled (see also in §126). The sense is the appointment of the two as chiefs over the rest; it does not say of what they are made elders.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:"

morph.gloss: Chinggis, a man's name (personal name; the name taken by Temüjin) [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qahan on-speaking:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spoke again:
sentences.n: basa 'again' (Ming 再) shows a second speech of the qan. Shiratori's quotation mark opens on the next word and runs to the end of the section.

sentences.t: Teṅgiri γažar-a küčü nemežü igeġegdeġesü

morph.gloss: Heaven, Tengri (the sky as a god) [天]
to protect, to help (stem inferred from the Ming 護助) [被護助呵]

sentences.l: "Heaven Earth-to strength adding, if-it-be-protected,
sentences.i: "If Heaven and Earth add strength to us and protect us,
sentences.n: Teṅgiri γažar-a küčü nemežü is 'Heaven, to the Earth, adding strength' (Ming 天地行氣力添着). The -a on γažar-a is 'to', as the Ming 行 marks, and so the line reads 'Heaven adds strength to the Earth'; I take the pair as one force that gives strength, and I read 'to us' in order to make a sense; the Ming has no 'us'. igeġegdeġesü is a passive of a stem igeġe- (inferred from the Ming 護助 'protect, help') with the conditional -ġesü: 'if it is protected'.

sentences.t: ta Žamuqa anda-ača nama-ji keġen sedkižü nököčešü keġen

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
sworn friend, blood-brother (Ming 契合) [(契合)處]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to be a companion (from nökör; stem inferred) [做伴我]
hortative: 'let ...' (uncertain; the Ming 做伴我 'let (them) be my companions')

sentences.l: you Jamuqa anda-from me 'let-them-be-companion-to-me' thinking, saying
sentences.i: you, thinking of me, saying 'let them be my companions' from Jamuqa the anda,
sentences.n: A hard line. Ming: 您人名契合處我行麽道想着做伴我麽道: 'you, from Jamuqa the anda, saying ‘to me’, thinking, saying ‘be companions to me’'. I read ta ... sedkižü nököčešü keġen as 'you, thinking ‘let them be companions to me’', with the speech or thought of the two men. nököčešü is nököče- 'be a companion' with an ending -šü that I take as a hortative from the Ming 做伴我; this ending is uncertain. The place of Jamuqa anda-ača is uncertain: either the people come from Jamuqa, or the thought is about Jamuqa. I leave the grammar as given and say that the line is not yet clear to me.

sentences.t: iregsed ötögüs ölže- ten nököd min-u ülü-ü boluγ̇užai ta" keġebe.

morph.gloss: good fortune, blessing (the first part of ölžeten; the line break splits the word) [吉慶]
possessive plural: 'those having' (plural of -tü/-tai; joins ölže-, 'those having blessing') [有的(每)]
genitive ending, set after its noun
particle of question (uncertain; the Ming puts its 麽 on the next word)
ending of the verb (uncertain; the Ming 做麽 reads it as a question, 'shall (they) become?')

sentences.l: come-ones old-men blessed companions my not-? become you," he-said.
sentences.i: the old men who came, blessed, my companions: will they not be mine, you?" he said.
sentences.n: iregsed ötögüs ölže- ten nököd min-u: 'the ones who came, the old men, the blessed (ölže + -ten 'having blessing'; Shiratori's line break splits the word), companions of mine'. boluγ̇užai ends in a form I cannot name; the Ming 不做麽 (not-become?) asks a question, so 'will they not become ...?'. I take it as 'my companions', and the speech as an appeal: those who came are mine, so you two, take them up. The sense of the whole speech from 'If Heaven and Earth' on is uncertain and I mark it so.

sentences.t: "Žüg žüg tüšibe tan-i."

morph.gloss: to entrust, to commit to (Ming 委付) [委付了]
you (stem of ta before a case ending) [您行]

sentences.l: "Each each entrusted you."
sentences.i: "I entrust you, each to his own place."
sentences.n: žüg žüg is 'each, each' (Ming 各各), žüg being 'side, direction'. tüšibe is tüši- 'entrust' (Ming 委付) in the past, and tan-i is 'you (acc.)'. The stem tüši- is attested here for the first time in the work. Whether it means 'put in charge' or 'rely on' is not settled; the Ming's 委付 is 'entrust'. The mark closes the speech and the section's long quotation.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)i qān bolγaba.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, a man's name (personal name; the name taken by Temüjin) [太祖︀]
accusative: marks the object (the (n) is Shiratori's)
qan, ruler (the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qahan-(acc.) qan he-caused-to-become.
sentences.i: They made Chinggis Qahan qan.
sentences.n: bolγaba is bol- 'become' + causative -γa- + -ba, 'made to become' (Ming 敎做了). The subject is not stated. The stop after bolγaba is Shiratori's; keġen in the next unit takes the sentence up as a quotation.

sentences.t: keġen Kereid-ün Toγ̇oril Qān-dur Daγai, Sükegei qojar-i elči ilebe.

morph.gloss: the Kereid, a people (the -d is probably plural) [種名(的)]

sentences.l: saying, the Kereid's To'oril Qan-to, Daqai, Sükegei two-(acc.) envoys he-sent.
sentences.i: Saying so, he sent Daqai and Sükegei as envoys to To'oril Qan of the Kereid.
sentences.n: keġen is keġe- 'say' + -n, 'saying' (Ming 麽道), the quotation marker that closes the speech. The envoys go to To'oril Qan: Kereid-ün Toγ̇oril Qān-dur 'the Kereid's To'oril Qan-to'. qojar-i 'the two' (Ming 兩箇行) is an accusative, 'sent the two as envoys'. ilebe is ile- (Ming 去了 'went') in the past; with elči 'envoy' and the accusative on the men I read 'sent'.

sentences.l: To'oril Qan Temüjin the son my qan to-be-made indeed right.
sentences.i: To'oril Qan said: "That Temüjin, my son, be made qan: that is right.
sentences.n: No speech verb stands here, but the Ming gives no sign of a break: To'oril Qan answers the envoys. köġün-i 'the son' (Ming 兒子行) is accusative, with Temüžin köġün-i as the object of bolγaqu, the future participle of the causative bol-γa-, 'to be made'. na is a particle for which the Ming has 好生 'good, well'; I do not know its force. žöb is 'right' (Ming 是). Shiratori has no opening mark here; the closing mark falls at the end of the speech after tamtuludqun.

sentences.t: Monγol qā ügeġün ker aqun ta.

morph.gloss: qa'an, sovereign (a short form of qaγan) [皇帝]
plural, 'those' (uncertain; the Ming 每 marks a plural)
ending of the verb (uncertain; the Ming 住麽 reads it as a question)

sentences.l: Mongols qa'an without-ones how dwell you.
sentences.i: How would you Mongols stay without a qa'an?
sentences.n: qā is a short form of qaγan, as qān is of the other, 'qa'an'; the Ming glosses 皇帝 again. ügeġün: ügei 'without' with an ending -ġün that the Ming's 每 shows to be a plural, 'the ones without a qa'an'. ker aqun ta 'how will you stay'; again aqun, now with the Ming 過的 'pass the time'.

sentences.t: Ene eje-ben bu ebdedkün;

morph.gloss: counsel, consultation, agreement (Ming 商量) [商量自的(行)]
prohibitive/imperative, second person plural (uncertain; the Ming 您 'you')

sentences.l: This counsel-one's-own do-not you-break;
sentences.i: Do not break this compact of yours;
sentences.n: eje-ben is eje 'counsel, agreement' (Ming 商量) + reflexive -ben, 'your own counsel'. bu ebdedkün: bu 'do not' with ebde- 'break' and an ending -dkün that I take as a plural prohibitive (Ming 您). 'Counsel' in the Ming sense is a consultation or compact; I render 'compact'.

sentences.t: eje žaṅgi-ban bu taludqun;

morph.gloss: counsel, consultation, agreement (Ming 商量) [商量]
bond, knot (Ming 結了的 'tied') [結了的 自的行]
to untie, to loosen (stem inferred from the Ming 解) [解了您]

sentences.l: counsel bond-one's-own do-not you-undo;
sentences.i: do not undo the bond of that compact;
sentences.n: žaṅgi is 'bond, knot' (Ming 結了的 'tied'); -ban is reflexive. taludqun is talu- 'untie, undo' (the stem is inferred from the Ming 解了) with the same plural prohibitive ending as the line before.

sentences.t: žaqa-ban bu tamtuludqun" keġežü iležü.

morph.gloss: collar (Ming 衣領) [衣領 自的行]
to tear (stem inferred from the Ming 扯) [扯了您]
to send, to go (the Ming glosses 去着 'going') [去着]

sentences.l: collar-one's-own do-not you-tear" saying he-sent.
sentences.i: do not tear the collar," he said, and sent them off.
sentences.n: žaqa-ban is 'one's own collar' (Ming 衣領). tamtuludqun is tamtulu- 'tear off' (stem inferred from the Ming 扯了) plus the same ending. The three prohibitions are a figure: a compact is a knot, a collar. keġežü iležü: 'saying, going/sending'; the Ming glosses iležü 去着 'going', and I take it as To'oril sending the envoys on their way.

sentences.t: Arγai-Qasar, Čaγ̇urqan qojar-i Žamuqa-dur elči ileġesü

morph.gloss: Arqai-Qasar, a man's name (personal name; Arγai 'Arqai' with Qasar) [人名]
Cha'urqan, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名 行]
to send (the Ming glosses 去 'go') [去呵]

sentences.l: Arqai-Qasar, Cha'urqan two-(acc.) Jamuqa-to envoys if-sent,
sentences.i: When Arqai-Qasar and Cha'urqan were sent to Jamuqa as envoys,
sentences.n: A converb chain starts here and goes on to the end of the speech: ileġesü is ile- 'send' + conditional -ġesü (Ming 去呵 'when sent'), 'when/if they were sent'. Arγai-Qasar is printed as one name with a hyphen, as in the prior part; the Ming glosses 人名 for both. The sentence has no stated subject.

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Jamuqa on-speaking:
sentences.i: Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: Jamuqa now speaks to the envoys (the next lines).

sentences.t: "Altan, Qučar qojar-a ügüle" keġen ügüležü ilerün;

morph.gloss: Altan, a man's name (personal name; the word means 'gold') [人名]
Quchar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to speak, to say (here the bare stem, imperative: 'say!') [說]
to send (the Ming glosses 去 'go') [去]

sentences.l: "Altan, Quchar two-to say" saying having-had-spoken on-sending;
sentences.i: "Say it to Altan and Quchar, the two," and, so saying, sending them off,
sentences.n: A message within a message. ügüle is the bare stem, an imperative 'say' (Ming 說); ügüležü keġen is 'saying it' and 'having had it said'. ilerün is ile- 'send' + -rün, 'on sending/going' (Ming 去). The Ming does not say whether Jamuqa speaks to the envoys or the envoys to Altan and Quchar.

sentences.t: "Altan, Qučar ta qojar Temüžin anda ba qojar žaγ̇ura Anda-jin

morph.gloss: Altan, a man's name (personal name; the word means 'gold') [人名]
Quchar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]
sworn friend, blood-brother (Ming 契合) [契合]
we (first-person plural pronoun; Ming 俺) [俺]
sworn friend, blood-brother (Ming 契合) [契合 的]

sentences.l: "Altan, Quchar, you two Temüjin anda we two between anda's
sentences.i: "Altan and Quchar, you two, between Temüjin the anda and us two, the anda's
sentences.n: A direct address to Altan and Quchar (Ming 您兩箇). ba qojar is 'we two' (Ming 俺兩箇); žaγ̇ura 'between' (Ming 間). Anda-jin is 'of the anda' (Ming 契合的), with a capital A in Shiratori's print. Shiratori puts a comma after Altan and a second after Qučar; it is not clear whether the anda-bond belongs to Temüjin or to both.

sentences.t: sübeġesečižü qabirγa qadqužu jakin qaγačaγ̇ulba ta.

morph.gloss: hollow of the flank, waist (Ming 腰窩) [腰窩戮着]
verb: to stab at (stem inferred from the Ming 戮)
to thrust in, to stab (Ming 插) [插着]
how, in what way (Ming 如何) [如何]

sentences.l: flank-stabbing rib thrusting how you-caused-to-part you.
sentences.i: stabbing the flank, thrusting at the rib: how did you part us?
sentences.n: sübeġesečižü is sübeġe 'flank, hollow of the waist' with a verb ending in -seči- that I take from the Ming 腰窩戮着 'stabbing the hollow of the waist'; the stem is inferred. qadqužu is qadqu- 'thrust in' (Ming 插着). Both belong to the figure of a knife into an anda's side, and mean 'parting two friends by treachery'. qaγačaγ̇ulba is qaγača- 'part' + causative -γ̇ul- + -ba, 'made part' (Ming 敎離了).

we (first-person plural pronoun; Ming 俺) [俺]

sentences.l: Anda we two-(acc.) not causing-to-part together when-we-were, Temüjin anda-(acc.) qan how not you-made, you.
sentences.i: While we two sworn friends were not yet parted, why did you not make Temüjin, the anda, qan? You.
sentences.n: ülü qaγačaγ̇ulun is 'not causing to part'; qamtu büküi- dür 'when being together' (Ming 一同有的時): the clause is 'when we, two, were together'. The Ming 不 attaches to qaγačaγ̇ulun. jakin ese bolγaba: 'how did you not make him qan' (Ming 如何不曾敎做了). Shiratori puts a stop after bolγaba and a lone ta. after it; I keep the two in one unit.

sentences.t: Edöġe ambar ele sedkil sedkižü qān bolγaba. ta.

morph.gloss: what, something (Ming 甚麽; sense uncertain) [甚麽]
emphatic particle: only, but, indeed (Ming 但) [但]
qan, ruler (the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Now what only heart having-thought qan you-made, you.
sentences.i: Now, with whatever thought in your hearts, you have made him qan, you.
sentences.n: ele is the emphatic particle (Ming 但 'only, but'); ambar I leave as the Ming gives it, 甚麽 'what'. Taken together, ambar ele sedkil sedkižü is 'thinking only what in the heart'. The line looks like a contrast to the one before: if you could have made him qan at the first, why only now?

sentences.t: Altan, Qučar ta qojar ügülegsen üges-tür(i)-jen kürün

sentences.l: Altan, Quchar you two the-said words-in-one's-own reaching
sentences.i: Altan and Quchar, you two, holding to the words you have said,
sentences.n: ügülegsen is ügüle- 'speak' + -gsen (Ming 說了的), 'what was said'. üges-tür(i)-jen is üge 'word' in the plural (-s) + -tür 'to, in' + reflexive -(i)jen: 'in/to your own words' (Ming 言語每裏自的行). kürün is kür- 'reach' + -ün (Ming 到): 'reaching to, keeping to'. The sense is that they must act up to what they promised; this is uncertain.

sentences.i: setting the anda's heart at rest,
sentences.n: amγ̇ulžu is the same verb as amuγ̇ulba in §125 (amu- + causative -γ̇ul-), written without the u; Shiratori prints it this way. anda-jin sedkil is 'the anda's heart'.

sentences.i: and be good companions to my anda," saying, and he sent them on.
sentences.n: anda-da 'to the anda' (Ming 契合行) with min-u 'my'. saiqatur is saiqan 'good' with an adverbial -tur (Ming 好好的); kü is the particle 'also, indeed'. nököčežü is nököče- 'be a companion' + -žü. ügüdkün is a form I take as 'give' (ögü-, Shiratori prints ügü-) with the plural imperative ending, 'give (it)': Ming 與您. Taken with nököčežü, 'give company' = 'be a companion'. keġežü iležü: 'saying, sent/going', as in §126.

sentences.n: bidan-u is bida 'we' + -n-u, 'our' (Ming 咱的): the Mongols' (the speaker's own camp, in the voice of the chronicle). Saγ̇ari-Keġer-e 'at Sa'ari-Ke'er' (Ming 地名行). bükü is bü- 'be' + -kü (Ming 有的). deġermedüre: deġermed- 'plunder' + a linking vowel + -re, a purposive 'to plunder' that I infer (Ming 搶劫). odčuγ̇ui is od- 'go' + -čuγ̇ui (Ming 去了來 'went and came').

sentences.n: deġermedčü abču odčuγ̇ui: 'plundering, taking, went'. Both converbs are in -čü/-ču, after a consonant stem. abču odčuγ̇ui 'took and went' (Ming 要着去了).

sentences.l: Jüchi-Darmala his-own-herd having-plundered gone, his-own-companions' heart being-unable,
sentences.i: Jüchi-Darmala's herd was plundered and gone, and his companions had not the heart to bear it,
sentences.n: A hard sentence. aduγ̇u-ban is the herd with reflexive -ban, 'his own herd'; deġermedčü odču is 'plundering, going', and the Ming 被搶着去着 reads it passively, 'being plundered, being gone'. nököd(i)-jen žürüge jadaγdažu is 'his own companions' heart being unable' (Ming 伴當每自的行心被不敢着); jada- 'be unable' is inferred from the Ming 不敢 'not dare', with the passive -γda-. I read 'his companions' hearts failed them'; the chain is uncertain.

sentences.n: mün is 'just, the very, himself' (Ming 只); nekežü is neke- 'attack, pursue' (Ming 襲着), a stem I do not know otherwise. Jüchi-Darmala goes after the raider.

sentences.i: and by night reached the edge of his own herd, lying flat along the mane of his own horse,
sentences.n: süni is 'night' (Ming 夜). aduγ̇un-u-γ̇an is aduγ̇un + genitive -u + reflexive -γ̇an, 'his own herd's'; kižiγ̇ar-a 'to the edge'. The horse is in the same case: morin-u-γ̇an del 'the mane of his own horse'. helige-ber(i)-jen kebtežü: kebte- 'lie down' and helige with the instrumental -ber and the reflexive; the Ming gives 伏臥 'lie prone' for helige-ber(i)-jen. helige is 'liver' elsewhere in this work, so the word here is uncertain: I give the Ming's sense.

sentences.i: came up, and shot Taichar through the backbone and killed him,
sentences.n: niruγ̇u in-ü: 'his spine' (Ming 脊梁他的), with the pronoun 'his' referring to Taichar. quγuru is quγu- 'break off' with -ru (Ming 斷), as in the earlier glossary; qarbužu is qarbu- 'shoot (an arrow)'. The sense is 'shooting the spine broken through', that is, shooting through the spine. alaγ̇ad is ala- 'kill' + -γ̇ad.

sentences.i: Jamuqa and those headed by him, the thirteen divisions of the Jadaran, banded together, becoming three tümens, and came over the Alaqiqud and the Turqaqud,
sentences.n: teriġüten is teriġü 'head' + plural possessive -ten, 'those having X at their head' (Ming 等項 'and the rest'). Žadaran harban γurban qarin is 'the Jadaran, thirteen divisions' (Ming 種名十三部); qarin, glossed 部, is not the qarin 'again' of other lines. The three tümens are three groups of ten thousand (Ming 三萬每). Alaγ̇iγ̇ud and Turqaγ̇ud(i)-jar are two mountain names (Ming 山名); -jar is an instrumental, 'by, along', and I read 'came over'.

sentences.l: together Onon's forest-in "let-us-feast" while-saying-together, at-the-feast
sentences.i: gathered together in the forest on the Onon, saying "Let us hold a feast," and holding the feast:
sentences.n: bolun is bol- with -un, 'together, all' (Ming 共). Onan-nu tün-dür is 'in the Onon's forest' (Ming 河名的林裏); the forms Onan and Onon are the same river. qurimlaja is qurimla- 'make a feast' with -ja, a hortative 'let us' (Ming 咱); keġeldüžü is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- + -žü, 'saying together' (Ming 共說着); qurimlarun is the same verb with -run, 'at the feasting'. The opening mark is at Onan-nu.

sentences.i: A jar was poured, beginning with Chinggis Qahan, Lady Högelün, Qasar, Sacha-Beki and the rest.
sentences.n: kiġed teriġülen: kiġed 'and others' (Ming 等) and teriġülen 'making X the head' (Ming 爲頭, from teriġü 'head'): the first jar starts with those named and goes round. The case endings are datives, -(n)a, -(n)e, -a, -de: 'for/to'. tüsürge is 'jar' (Ming 甕), tüsürčüġüi 'poured' (Ming 傾了). No subject is given.

sentences.n: basa 'again' (Ming 再). üčüġügen eke is 'little mother' (Ming 小娘), that is a junior wife or a mother's younger partner of Sacha-Beki; I leave it as given. Ebegei-ji teriġülen 'taking Ebegei as head' (Ming 額別該行爲頭). tüsürküi-jin tula: participle -küi + genitive -jin + tula 'because of' (Ming 傾了的上頭 'on account of the pouring').

sentences.i: said, "How is it that you pour, not beginning with me, but beginning with Ebegei?"

sentences.l: "Yesügei-Ba'atur, Negün-Taishi two-(acc.) of-dying because, thus being-beaten my what?"
sentences.i: "Because Yesügei-Ba'atur and Negün-Taishi, the two, are dead, I am beaten like this: what is mine?"
sentences.n: üküküi-jin tula is ükü- 'die' + participle -küi + genitive -jin + tula 'because of' (Ming 死的上頭): 'on account of the two having died'. qojar-i is the accusative of the two, as in other lines. ein is 'thus' (Ming 這般), ašigiγdaqui 'being beaten' (Ming 被打的), min-u jaγ̇un 'my what' (Ming 我的甚麽). I read it as a lament, 'what have I now?' but the force of min-u jaγ̇un is uncertain.

sentences.i: So he spoke, and wept aloud.
sentences.n: keġeġed is keġe- 'say' + -ġed. jeke daγ̇u-bar is 'great voice-with' (Ming 大聲依着), 'with a loud voice'. uilažuγ̇ui is uila- 'weep' + -žuγ̇ui (Ming 哭了). The mark closes the speech at jaγ̇un.
